thread:
mia: heads up — a customer (TKT-4832) reported we applied a voucher instead of issuing a refund. they were billed for $42.50 after our agent said refund processed. can someone triage?

sam: can you paste the original API call or support payload? router logs would be ideal.

mia: paste below. this is the /support/resolve call from our UI that should pick payments.issue_refund but router picked promotions.apply_voucher instead.
```
POST /v1/support/resolve
{
  "customer_id": "cust_789",
  "action": "refund",
  "amount": 42.50,
  "currency": "USD",
  "reason": "order canceled",
  "note": "refund to original payment method"
}
```

mia: router decision log snippet (redacted):
```
{ "request_id": "r-1345", "tool_chosen": "promotions.apply_voucher", "score": 0.63, "signals": ["has_amount", "has_reason", "action_refund_alias"] }
```

sam: wow. that score is pretty high. do we have the tool signatures? my suspicion: both tools accept a numeric field named amount/value and an optional note, causing ambiguous signature matching.

jordan: filing as P1 since it's customer-impacting billing. what region did this happen in?

mia: us-east-1. customer wants refund now. they were charged; txn id txn_44B. support already created a manual refund and notified them, but we need root cause and prevent recurrence.

ashley: looped in payments and routing. quick mitigation: can we add an override in autorouter for requests coming from /support/resolve to prioritize payments.issue_refund?

sam: yes we can add a short-lived route rule. i'll push a canary rule: if source=="support_ui" && intent contains "refund" -> force payments.issue_refund. deploying now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: router-rule-add #RR-987 by sam at 2026-04-21T15:12:03Z

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: router-rule-add #RR-987 at 2026-04-21T15:13:10Z

sam: mitigation in place. next steps: capture the decision_context for similar incidents and add disambiguation to our tool signatures: change promotions.apply_voucher signature to require "voucher_code" or "voucher_type" field, instead of accepting generic amount-only calls.

mia: agree. can you add a quick Kusto/SQL query to find other recent router_decision events where tool_chosen!=payments.issue_refund but request_source=="support_ui" and text contains "refund"? need list to notify affected customers.

sam: running query now. snippet: 
```
SELECT top 50 request_id, tool_chosen, score, payload
FROM router_decisions
WHERE source = 'support_ui' AND payload LIKE '%refund%' AND first_seen > ago(30d)
ORDER BY first_seen desc
```

sam: found 7 similar picks in the last 30d (all low-mid score 0.5-0.7). exporting IDs to #support-alerts.

jordan: file a follow-up EPIC with payments and routing to improve signature/schemas and add unit tests to the autorouter to catch ambiguous matches. also add a telemetry alert when a tool with overlapping signature reaches >3 misroutes in 24h.

ashley: notes for postmortem: 1) ambiguous parameter names (amount/value) 2) shared optional fields across promo/refund 3) lack of context-scoped routing rules for support flows.

mia: customer updated and manual refunds issued. requesting ETA for a permanent fix.

sam: timeline: small signature change + unit tests -> 2 business days. schema change for promotions tool (require voucher_code) -> 1 week with testing. I'll post PRs in the routing repo shortly.

mia: thanks. can we also add a short playbook entry to support runbook: if router selects promotions.apply_voucher for refund intents, 1) don't confirm to customer, 2) escalate to payments, 3) issue manual refund.

ashley: added runbook item. linking to TKT-4832 and RR-987.

mia: any blockers from SRE/security?

jordan: none. just remind folks to include audit logs when we change signature enforcement so we can rollback cleanly.

sam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/router/pull/421 — adds require_field: voucher_code on promotions.apply_voucher and a unit test for support_ui -> payments.issue_refund priority.

mia: great. we'll monitor #support-alerts for any new hits. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
